Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are the operations director at HARBOR OAKS PET LODGE, a pet boarding and daycare chain with six locations. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend whether the chain should change how its play yards are staffed, after two quarters in which a newer competitor took bookings the lodge had held for years.

After a dog was hurt in a yard two years ago, the lodge wrote a rule that two attendants stay in every play group with their phones put away. Those attendants know the dogs by name and write the daily note each owner reads at pickup, and that is what the lodge is known for.

BRIGHT PAWS PET CLUB runs one attendant to a yard and covers the rest with ceiling cameras that stream to a phone app, and it charges less. Customers have begun asking for the same feed. Cameras and a single attendant would let the lodge match that price, and would end the second attendant, the phones-away rule and the daily notes with it.

The owner (judge) wants you to recommend one course and to say how the attendants would be told. Keeping the rule leaves the lodge above the competitor's price with no feed to offer. You will present in the owner's (judge) office. The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you for your work after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of HARBOR OAKS PET LODGE. Business background is the same as the situation above. The staffing rule you wrote after the injury is the most expensive thing the lodge does, and it is also the reason customers say they come.

You want the operations director to recommend how the play yards should be staffed and to say how that decision would be told to the attendants it changes.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would tell us early that it was not?
